provenance: Newly authored practice questions based on the user-supplied topic outline; checked against primary technical documentation. These are not reconstructed verbatim exam questions.

questions.prompt: A team stores a Dockerfile in a supported GitHub repository. Every push to main must build and publish an image to Azure Container Registry without maintaining a separate build server. Which TWO features should it configure?
questions.explanation: An ACR Task supplies the managed build execution; its source-commit trigger starts a run when the configured branch changes. Geo-replication distributes registry content across regions. Scope maps constrain repository token permissions; neither detects commits or runs builds. Repository webhook authorization is also required.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: An ACR Task with that repository as its source context
A source-commit trigger for the task
Geo-replication for the registry
A repository scope map

questions.prompt: An existing Container App must receive a Key Vault secret through a platform-managed secret reference. The vault uses Azure RBAC and is reachable. A system identity has not yet been enabled. Select the THREE required actions in dependency order.
answer: Enable the Container App system-assigned managed identity
Grant that identity Key Vault Secrets User on the required secret scope
Create a Key Vault-backed Container Apps secret using that identity and reference it from an environment variable
questions.explanation: The identity must exist before its principal can receive a role assignment. The secret reference then uses the authorized identity to resolve the vault value. A registry admin account grants no Key Vault access. A Dockerfile value embeds the secret in image configuration. Allow time for role propagation.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Create a Key Vault-backed Container Apps secret using that identity and reference it from an environment variable
Grant that identity Key Vault Secrets User on the required secret scope
Enable the Container App system-assigned managed identity
Enable the ACR admin account to read Key Vault
Write the secret value into the Dockerfile

questions.prompt: Custom events contain a subject such as /uploads/ai/report-42 and a data.fileType property. Deliver only events whose subject starts with /uploads/ai/ AND whose fileType is pdf. Preserve failed deliveries after their retry policy is exhausted. Select each setting.
answer: Subject begins with /uploads/ai/
Advanced StringIn filter on data.fileType with value pdf
An authorized Azure Blob Storage container
questions.explanation: The subject prefix and data-property filter are separate conditions. An event-type filter does not inspect a path, and a suffix does not inspect data.fileType. Event Grid writes undeliverable events to its configured Blob destination; a Service Bus DLQ is not this setting. Configure storage access as well.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
questions.reviewNote: A subject filter alone cannot enforce fileType=pdf; the supplied outline omitted the advanced filter.
rows: Advanced StringIn filter on data.fileType with value pdf
An authorized Azure Blob Storage container

questions.prompt: A valid API key was committed to a public Git repository. The goal is to make that exposed credential unusable. Proposed solution: delete the value from the latest source file and put the SAME key in a GitHub Actions repository secret, without revoking it. Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Moving the key to an encrypted CI secret does not invalidate copies already in history, clones or logs. Revoke or rotate the exposed key first and address retained sensitive data as appropriate. Repository secrets can protect future workflow use; they are not inherently unsuitable.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Yes
No
questions.reviewNote: The No answer is about an already leaked key that remains valid, not a blanket rejection of GitHub secrets.

questions.prompt: The same image digest must run in development and production. Endpoint URLs and an API secret must vary by environment without rebuilding the image or embedding the secret. Proposed solution: set both values as literal ENV instructions in the Dockerfile. Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Dockerfile ENV values become image configuration and travel with the image. A literal secret is exposed, and changing baked values requires a new build. Inject non-secret settings and securely resolved secrets at deployment/runtime instead. Environment variables themselves are a valid runtime interface; the problem is baking the values into the image.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Yes
No

questions.prompt: An App Service container must obtain its API key from Key Vault using its managed identity, with no secret value in the image. Proposed solution: copy the key into a Dockerfile ENV instruction and deploy the resulting image. Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: The application would read a baked value, not retrieve it using the managed identity. Configure a Key Vault reference in an App Service setting and authorize the app identity instead. The platform-resolved value is still present in application memory/environment, so application logging must not reveal it.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Yes
No

questions.prompt: An ACA worker must scale from the length of the Azure Storage queue image-jobs. Authentication, accountName and queueLength are already configured. Fill the two remaining custom scale-rule fields; replica bounds are configured separately.
answer: azure-queue
image-jobs
questions.explanation: The azure-queue scaler targets Storage Queue length, and queueName identifies the queue. azure-servicebus selects a different messaging service; cpu measures container utilization. minReplicas and maxReplicas are scale bounds, not the queue name. A usable rule also needs authentication, the account and a target queue length.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
questions.reviewNote: The original two-field summary is valid only when the other required scaler settings are supplied.

questions.prompt: A Python service on ACA must retrieve a Key Vault secret directly with SecretClient, without application credentials. The vault uses Azure RBAC. The design explicitly chooses a system-assigned identity. Which THREE actions meet the design?
questions.explanation: The identity supplies a token, Secrets User authorizes secret-value reads, and SecretClient performs retrieval. Key Vault Reader can read metadata but not secret contents. A baked secret defeats the design. A user-assigned identity or platform Key Vault reference can also work in other designs; this question explicitly selects the system identity and SDK path.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Enable the app system-assigned managed identity
Assign Key Vault Secrets User to that principal at an appropriate scope
Use SecretClient with an Azure Identity credential that selects that managed identity
Bake the secret value into the image
Grant the app the Key Vault Reader role only

questions.prompt: An ACA HTTP API must keep stable and candidate revisions active, send 10% of ordinary traffic to the candidate, and let testers address the candidate at a stable revision-specific URL. Complete the design.
answer: Multiple
Assign a revision label to the candidate
Set stable/candidate revision weights to 90/10
questions.explanation: Multiple revision mode permits concurrent active revisions and weighted traffic. A label provides a direct URL for its assigned revision and does not itself set the percentage sent by the normal app URL. Single mode cannot keep both revisions active for this weighted rollout; an image tag is not a revision-routing control.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
rows: Assign a revision label to the candidate
Replace the stable image tag with latest
A revision label automatically routes 10% of ordinary traffic

questions.prompt: An ACA workload already has a managed identity and registry authentication configured. Its ACR uses RBAC Registry + ABAC Repository Permissions mode. The app only needs to pull a known repository image. Which role grants the required repository data access?
questions.explanation: Container Registry Repository Reader grants image pull access in an ABAC-enabled registry. Generic Reader grants control-plane visibility, not image data access. Legacy AcrPull and AcrPush are not honored in this registry mode. In a classic RBAC-only registry, AcrPull is the usual pull role. Repository catalog listing is unnecessary when the image path is already known.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Container Registry Repository Reader
Reader on the registry resource
AcrPull
AcrPush
questions.reviewNote: Corrected the incomplete role name: Container Registry Repository Reader, with registry permission mode made explicit.

questions.prompt: An App Service container needs a non-secret region label and an API secret stored in Key Vault. It reads both from environment variables. The app identity has vault access. Choose the simplest setting for each.
answer: A plain App Service app setting
A Key Vault reference in an App Service app setting
questions.explanation: Ordinary app settings are suitable for a non-secret label. A Key Vault reference lets the platform resolve the secret using the app identity. Storing a region in Key Vault can technically work but adds unnecessary secret management under the simplest-setting requirement. Baking the API key into the Dockerfile violates secret separation.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
questions.reviewNote: A Key Vault reference for non-secret data is unnecessary here, not technically impossible.
rows: A plain App Service app setting
A Key Vault secret and reference
A Key Vault reference in an App Service app setting
A literal API key in the Dockerfile

questions.prompt: A Linux custom-container web app writes diagnostics to stdout/stderr. Container filesystem logging is disabled. Choose the TWO commands, in order, to enable it and watch new messages from the live stream.
answer: az webapp log config --resource-group rg-lab --name lab-api --docker-container-logging filesystem
az webapp log tail --resource-group rg-lab --name lab-api
questions.explanation: log config enables capture and log tail opens the stream. log show reports logging configuration; it does not stream application output. Activity logs describe Azure control-plane operations, not the container stdout/stderr stream.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: az monitor activity-log list --resource-group rg-lab
az webapp log config --resource-group rg-lab --name lab-api --docker-container-logging filesystem
az webapp log tail --resource-group rg-lab --name lab-api
az webapp log show --resource-group rg-lab --name lab-api

questions.prompt: A release must refer to the identical container image manifest even if someone later moves a registry tag. Which image reference satisfies this requirement?
questions.explanation: A digest identifies image content; moving a tag does not change the content addressed by that digest. A latest tag, a bare repository reference and a writable random tag can resolve to different content later. Digest pinning does not stop deletion of the image, so retention and registry access still matter.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: A repository reference ending in @sha256:<manifest-digest>
The repository latest tag
The repository name without a tag or digest
A randomly named tag whose write permissions remain enabled

questions.prompt: An AKS pod repeatedly enters CrashLoopBackOff. You do not yet know whether its application exits, a probe fails or it exceeds a memory limit. What is the best first diagnostic action?
questions.explanation: Pod events, termination state and kubectl logs --previous preserve evidence about the failure. More replicas usually repeat the same defect. Shortening a liveness delay can increase premature restarts. Draining a node before identifying a node fault is disruptive and may obscure evidence.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Increase the Deployment replica count
Shorten the liveness probe initial delay
Drain and reboot the node immediately
Inspect pod events and container termination details, and retrieve previous-container logs

questions.prompt: A team wants an ACR Task to run nightly, build when main changes, and rebuild when its tracked base image is updated. Which THREE trigger types support these requirements?
questions.explanation: Timers schedule runs; source triggers respond to configured repository updates; base-image triggers rebuild tracked dependencies after relevant updates. Portal sign-in is not an ACR Task trigger. A nightly timer is useful for scheduled work but does not replace commit detection.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Timer trigger
Source-code commit trigger
Base-image update trigger
An administrator signing in to the Azure portal

questions.prompt: AKS events repeatedly show liveness-probe failures during model loading. The pod has restarted several times, but the logs from the previous container have not been read. Which next step is most useful before changing the deployment?
questions.explanation: Correlate previous logs and events with probe thresholds to establish whether slow startup is being mistaken for a hang. A startup probe may then protect initialization, but investigate first. Decreasing the delay worsens premature checks; extra replicas and node reboots do not correct a probe configuration. This scenario distinguishes the repeated troubleshooting topic from item 14.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Inspect previous-container logs and probe timing against the model startup duration
Decrease initialDelaySeconds to detect the failure faster
Scale to ten replicas
Reboot every cluster node

questions.prompt: An ACA HTTP app is running, but ingress is disabled. You own api.example.com and want an automatically renewed managed certificate. Select the FOUR stages in dependency order; each stage includes the related verification it names.
answer: Enable HTTP ingress and ensure the app can be reached for certificate validation
Create the required CNAME and TXT DNS records and wait for them to resolve
Add and validate api.example.com on the container app
Provision the managed certificate and bind the validated hostname
questions.explanation: Ingress and the required public validation path must work first. DNS records establish routing and domain ownership; hostname validation precedes certificate issuance/binding. A certificate cannot be issued for an unvalidated hostname in this workflow. Registry anonymous pull has no role in domain validation. Keep certificate prerequisites valid for renewals.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Create the required CNAME and TXT DNS records and wait for them to resolve
Provision the managed certificate and bind the validated hostname
Add and validate api.example.com on the container app
Enable HTTP ingress and ensure the app can be reached for certificate validation
Enable anonymous access to the container registry
Issue and bind the certificate before configuring DNS
questions.reviewNote: Corrected the supplied order: managed certificate → binding → DNS → validation was reversed. Ingress is a prerequisite, not a distractor.

questions.prompt: Every Function App environment must have the same reviewed infrastructure definition, deployed automatically after an approved repository change. Which approach best meets BOTH declarative infrastructure and automated deployment requirements?
questions.explanation: Bicep expresses the desired resource configuration; the pipeline executes a reviewed deployment. CLI is useful for invoking Bicep but an imperative-only script does not meet this stated declarative requirement. Portal creation and manual code publishing do not provide the required reproducible infrastructure pipeline.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Keep Bicep templates in Git and deploy them through GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines
Maintain an imperative Azure CLI script with no infrastructure template
Create resources manually in the portal
Publish application code manually from a developer laptop

questions.prompt: When a blob is created, two independent Azure Functions must receive a routed notification without polling storage. You want to subscribe to the storage service native events rather than have the uploader send an extra request. Which service provides that routing?
questions.explanation: Event Grid can subscribe to the storage system topic and route BlobCreated events to handlers. An HTTP endpoint alone does not subscribe itself to storage events. Storage queues and Service Bus topics can carry work when a producer sends it, but do not by themselves subscribe to the native Blob event stream.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Azure Event Grid
An HTTP-triggered Function alone
An Azure Storage queue alone
A Service Bus topic alone
questions.reviewNote: All four technologies can participate in workflows; the new stem specifies native Blob events to make Event Grid uniquely appropriate.

questions.prompt: For the Fabrikam maintenance library, select the FOUR stages in dependency order to enable vector storage and an HNSW retrieval path. After deployment, verify the query plan and filtered-search recall.
answer: Enable the vector extension in this database
Add an embedding vector(1536) column and populate it with the chosen model
Create an HNSW index on embedding using vector_cosine_ops
Run an ascending embedding <=> query with trusted tenant/date predicates and LIMIT
questions.explanation: The database needs the extension before it can use vector types, and the column must exist before its index can be created. vector_cosine_ops matches the cosine-distance operator <=>. A B-tree can help scalar filters but does not replace the vector ANN index. With approximate indexes, filtering can reduce returned candidates; tune iterative scans/candidate search or use exact retrieval when required.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Create the vector column before enabling the extension
Use a B-tree on embedding as the approximate-nearest-neighbor index
Enable the vector extension in this database
Run an ascending embedding <=> query with trusted tenant/date predicates and LIMIT
Add an embedding vector(1536) column and populate it with the chosen model
Create an HNSW index on embedding using vector_cosine_ops
questions.reviewNote: The setup order is an implementation dependency, not a claim that filtered HNSW always returns the exact nearest neighbors.

caseData.Overview: Fabrikam stores maintenance-manual chunks in an existing PostgreSQL documents table. Each row has a tenant_id, a publication timestamp and text. A trusted ingestion service generates 1,536-dimensional embeddings with one fixed model.
caseData.Requirements: Use cosine distance for approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval. Results must be filtered to the authenticated tenant and an allowed publication date range. The vector extension is available on the server but is not yet enabled in this database. Authorization derives the tenant from the authenticated identity, never directly from a caller-supplied tenant field.

questions.prompt: A Redis search service receives 1,536-dimensional query vectors encoded as little-endian float32 bytes. The requirements specify approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval over a large corpus. Choose the matching index settings.
answer: VECTOR
HNSW
FLOAT32
questions.explanation: VECTOR declares a vector-search field. HNSW provides approximate retrieval; FLAT is valid vector search but performs exact brute-force search and does not satisfy this ANN requirement. FLOAT32 matches the query encoding; FLOAT64 needs a different byte layout and size. TEXT and TAG fields do not define vector distance search.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
questions.reviewNote: FLAT and FLOAT64 are supported choices in other designs; they are wrong here because ANN and float32 input are explicit.

questions.prompt: A RAG service may reuse a response for at most 24 hours. Document updates must never cause retrieval to use an embedding for an older document version. Choose a response policy and an update protocol. Writers can enforce a version check before retrieval uses a cached embedding.
answer: Set an absolute 24-hour TTL when the response is written
Invalidate/version-check on document writes and regenerate before the new version is eligible for retrieval
questions.explanation: An absolute TTL bounds a response lifetime from its write; sliding expiry can keep it much longer. Embedding freshness requires coordination with document versions. Invalidation alone can have races, so reject stale versions and wait or regenerate on a miss. A response TTL does not update a separate embedding cache, and permanent ID-only entries hide revisions.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
questions.reviewNote: Added version/race handling: an asynchronous invalidation event alone cannot guarantee that embeddings are always current.
rows: Set an absolute 24-hour TTL when the response is written
Renew the 24-hour TTL on every read
Invalidate/version-check on document writes and regenerate before the new version is eligible for retrieval
Cache each embedding forever under only its document ID
Rely only on the response TTL

questions.prompt: A partner API credential is stored as a Key Vault SECRET. The partner supports replacement credentials. It must be rotated every 30 days; consumers must pick up the current enabled version without code changes. Which TWO measures are required?
questions.explanation: Secret rotation must update the issuing system as well as Key Vault. A versionless read can obtain the latest secret, but clients must refresh cached values and coordinate overlap/revocation. Key rotation policies apply to cryptographic keys, not arbitrary API secrets. A pinned version never switches automatically. Versionless retrieval does not search backward if the latest version is disabled.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Schedule automation that rotates the credential at the partner and stores the replacement as a new secret version
Read a versionless secret name and use a controlled refresh policy during rollout
Configure a Key Vault cryptographic-key rotation policy on this secret
Pin the original secret version in all clients
questions.reviewNote: Corrected the supplied answer: a key rotation policy is not a general API-secret rotation mechanism. The 30-day interval is a workload requirement, not a Key Vault default.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL application must rank documents by cosine similarity and filter by an exact publication-time range. It uses pgvector, and the embedding model outputs 768 components. Which TWO schema choices support these operations directly?
questions.explanation: A vector column supports pgvector distance operators with a fixed dimension. A timestamp type supports chronological comparisons and validation of time values. Arbitrary text requires parsing/casting and is not directly a typed vector. Free-form dates can sort lexicographically rather than chronologically and admit invalid or ambiguous formats. Appropriate vector and scalar indexes are separate performance decisions.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Store embeddings in a vector(768) column
Store publication times in a typed timestamptz column
Store vectors only as arbitrary varchar text
Store publication times as unvalidated free-form strings

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB for NoSQL container holds JSON documents. New writes must include tip as a JSON number, and a query over legacy records must return only records with a numeric tip. Choose the correct mechanism for each requirement.
answer: Validate presence and numeric type in the application write path
WHERE IS_DEFINED(c.tip) AND IS_NUMBER(c.tip)
questions.explanation: An indexing policy controls how properties are indexed, not whether writes conform to a required schema. Validate at each authorized write entry point to reject missing or non-numeric values. IS_NUMBER excludes strings, null and other non-number types; IS_DEFINED makes the presence check explicit. Presence alone admits strings, and ordering does not filter invalid values.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
questions.reviewNote: Corrected the supplied answer: an index cannot enforce that tip is present and numeric.
rows: Add a Number index on /tip/? to enforce the document schema
Validate presence and numeric type in the application write path

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB account, database appdb and container documents already exist. Endpoint and credentials are available. Arrange the FOUR client operations needed to query the container with the synchronous Python SDK.
answer: Construct CosmosClient for the account endpoint
Obtain the database client with get_database_client("appdb")
Obtain the container client with get_container_client("documents")
Call query_items and iterate its results
questions.explanation: CosmosClient provides database proxies; a DatabaseProxy provides container proxies; ContainerProxy exposes query_items. These get-client calls do not provision the existing resources. Account creation and upsert are unnecessary for reading. Parameters, partition targeting, authentication and iteration still need to match the query.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Upsert a new document before every read
Obtain the database client with get_database_client("appdb")
Create a new Cosmos DB account first
Obtain the container client with get_container_client("documents")
Construct CosmosClient for the account endpoint
Call query_items and iterate its results

questions.prompt: In the current Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos .NET SDK, an account and its data resources already exist. Select the THREE objects used in order to reach an existing container from an account endpoint.
answer: CosmosClient
Database returned by GetDatabase
Container returned by GetContainer

Reading an item then uses the Container and its item ID plus partition key. Do not mix .NET object names with Python proxy names.

AccountClient
CosmosClient
Database returned by GetDatabase
Container returned by GetContainer

answer: CosmosClient
DatabaseProxy

options: CosmosClient
ContainerProxy
DocumentClient as the current top-level v4 API
DatabaseProxy

questions.prompt: The resource group, Cosmos DB for NoSQL account and appdb database exist. The signed-in identity can create containers, the account supports provisioned throughput, and documents does not exist. Does this command create documents with a /tenantId partition key and dedicated 400 RU/s throughput?
questions.explanation: New-AzCosmosDBSqlContainer creates the SQL/NoSQL container under the specified database. Hash and /tenantId set the partition key; Throughput supplies provisioned RU/s for the container. The statement assumes an eligible account and sufficient permissions; it is not a command to create the account itself.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Yes
No
questions.reviewNote: The original item had no complete command or answer; this is a new, fully specified PowerShell scenario.

questions.prompt: A chatbot searches an Azure AI Search index populated with 1,536-dimensional embeddings from model A. It must retrieve semantically related chunks and return only documents authorized for the authenticated tenant. Choose each query configuration.
answer: Use model A and the same embedding configuration used during indexing
Apply a tenant filter derived from trusted authentication context
Return an explicit insufficient-evidence response
questions.explanation: Query and indexed embeddings must occupy the same vector space, not merely have a convenient size. Derive the tenant constraint from trusted authorization data. Retrieval can fail to provide evidence; the response policy must support abstention. An embedding-model mismatch damages retrieval, user-controlled tenant selection bypasses isolation, and plausible generation is not grounded evidence.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
questions.reviewNote: The source exposed only a topic. This authored question supplies model compatibility, authorization and missing-evidence requirements.
rows: Use model A and the same embedding configuration used during indexing
Apply a tenant filter derived from trusted authentication context
Accept any tenant ID supplied in the user prompt
Present a plausible answer as a verified document fact

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB for NoSQL container already has a valid vector embedding policy and enough populated vectors for the chosen index. Vector queries currently scan without a vector index and consume excessive RUs per query. You need an approximate search index. Which change addresses the missing capability?
questions.explanation: The vector index supplies an approximate similarity-search access path; its path and embedding policy must agree. Strong consistency does not create an index and can cost more for reads. More provisioned throughput may reduce throttling but does not eliminate a scan or lower its per-query work. Partition design can help scoping but is not a substitute for the missing vector index.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Add a supported vectorIndexes entry such as diskANN or quantizedFlat with the correct vector path
Switch every read to Strong consistency
Increase provisioned RU/s without adding an index
Choose a new partition key without configuring vector indexing

questions.prompt: An existing Cosmos DB for NoSQL query is SELECT * FROM c ORDER BY c.rating DESC, c.createdAt DESC. Its required composite index is missing. Which proposed index supports this two-property ORDER BY?
questions.explanation: A matching composite index preserves the property sequence and compatible direction combination for a multi-property ORDER BY. A one-property composite or independent range indexes do not supply that ordering. More RU/s cannot replace the missing required index. An index with both directions reversed can also support this query; it is deliberately not offered as a wrong option.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: A composite index with /rating descending followed by /createdAt descending
A composite index with only /createdAt descending
Two separate single-property range indexes alone
Disable indexing and increase RU/s
questions.reviewNote: Clarified that all-opposite sort directions can also be supported; descending is not the only possible valid index.

questions.prompt: A Python service uses Psycopg 3 to read an order by a user-supplied ID. Select the THREE fragments in order to build a parameterized query call. The table name is fixed by the application.
answer: Define sql = "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = %s"
Bind params = (order_id,) as a one-element tuple
Call cursor.execute(sql, params)
questions.explanation: Psycopg passes values separately from SQL using placeholders and a parameter sequence; the trailing comma makes a one-element tuple. Concatenation permits SQL injection, and quoting the placeholder breaks parameter binding. Values use placeholders; dynamic identifiers need Psycopg SQL composition rather than value placeholders.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Call cursor.execute(sql, params)
Concatenate order_id into the SQL string
Quote the %s placeholder inside the SQL text
Define sql = "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = %s"
Bind params = (order_id,) as a one-element tuple

questions.prompt: A RAG team stores 50,000 supported PDFs in Azure Blob Storage. It wants a managed pipeline to extract text, split it into chunks and create searchable embeddings with minimal custom ingestion code. What should it configure?
questions.explanation: Integrated vectorization connects supported data sources, document processing, chunking, embedding and indexing. A custom pipeline can work but conflicts with the minimal-custom-code objective. Stored procedures and cross-partition queries do not provide the requested managed PDF vectorization pipeline. Model quotas, supported file formats, OCR needs and indexer scheduling still need configuration.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: An Azure AI Search indexer and skillset with chunking and embedding skills, writing to a vector index
A hand-written extraction, batching and embedding pipeline for every PDF
Cosmos DB stored procedures to parse all PDFs
A cross-partition database query with no ingestion pipeline
questions.reviewNote: The corpus size alone does not guarantee capacity; the stem specifies the ingestion capability and optimization goal.

questions.prompt: A manual has 40,000 tokens, much more than the selected embedding model accepts in one request. Answers often require paragraphs that cross page boundaries. Which strategy is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Bounded chunks meet model limits, and overlap can preserve context split across neighboring chunks. Tune size and overlap using retrieval evaluation. A single oversized request is invalid; fixed page boundaries can exceed limits or break concepts. Model memory cannot replace retrieval of this private manual. One embedding per page can be valid for some documents, but the stated page-boundary and size requirements make it a poor universal rule here.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Split by useful semantic boundaries into token-bounded chunks with modest overlap and retain source metadata
Submit the entire manual as one embedding request
Always use exactly one embedding per physical page regardless of its length or content
Skip document ingestion and rely on the chat model memory

questions.prompt: A non-HTTP ACA worker processes a Service Bus queue. It may wait for event-driven cold starts and must run no worker replicas while the queue is empty. Which configuration satisfies this replica requirement?
questions.explanation: The queue scaler can detect work when no worker replica is running and request scale-out. minReplicas=0 permits scale-in to zero. CPU-only scaling cannot observe queued work while no replica is active; the other choices retain compute. This reduces worker replica usage, but messaging, networking and other platform charges may still apply.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: A Service Bus KEDA scale rule with minReplicas set to 0 and authorized queue access
A CPU-only scale rule with minReplicas set to 1
An AKS Deployment using an ordinary CPU HPA alone
Five fixed ACA replicas
questions.reviewNote: Zero replicas does not imply zero total Azure cost.

questions.prompt: Users ask exact totals and date-range comparisons over a frequently updated finance workbook. An ingestion job can validate its rows. The assistant must compute from current authorized records, not estimate from prose. Which design best meets the requirement?
questions.explanation: Structured queries compute aggregations over the applicable rows; a tool schema lets the assistant request those operations. The application must validate arguments and enforce authorization. Embeddings can help locate explanatory text but do not ensure complete exact aggregations. Pretraining cannot know the current private workbook, and unverified image interpretation is not a reliable aggregation engine.
questions.origin: Original scenario based on the supplied 59-topic outline
options: Load validated typed rows into a structured store and expose constrained parameterized aggregation tools to the agent
Embed the workbook text and ask the model to guess the total from retrieved excerpts
Ask the model to use knowledge learned during pretraining

questions.prompt: A worker uses PeekLock to process purchase messages. Its business operation can fail, and duplicate delivery is possible. Judge each proposed approach.
